target.title: fix(google-meet): keep Meet sessions on the agent that joined them
target.body:
Related: #77753
Related: #77763

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google Meet Chrome sessions could speak or consult as the wrong agent after delayed bridge startup or same-tab reuse in a multi-agent deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Meet now resolves one canonical agent owner when a session is created, stores that owner on the session, and reuses it for every later bridge startup and probe. When a live Chrome talk-back tab is reused by another agent, the runtime ends the previous bridge first so one browser tab cannot keep two agent contexts attached at once.

## User Impact

Multi-agent Google Meet calls stay on the agent that joined them across delayed admission, retries, and later speech checks. Reassigning the same live Chrome Meet tab to another agent now cleanly ends the previous talk-back bridge instead of leaving both agents attached to the same participant audio.

## Evidence

- Root cause: the session reuse path, delayed `#ensureChromeRealtimeBridge()` path, and `test_listen` tool hop in `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts` and `extensions/google-meet/index.ts` did not share one canonical session owner after per-agent routing was added in #77763.
- Provenance: #77763 made the bug visible by introducing per-agent Google Meet routing; the delayed bridge restart path itself dates to `88b983a713`.
- Focused AWS Crabbox proof: `corepack pnpm test extensions/google-meet/index.test.ts extensions/google-meet/src/cli.test.ts` (`run_ee008c8f9780`, 147 tests passed).
- Changed-gate AWS Crabbox proof: `env OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 corepack pnpm check:changed` (`run_b8ab53072915`, passed).
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
